tables.title: Blob creation steps for ECDSA signature (CCOP = 0b110000<i>0)
tables.text_helper: Table 189, "Blob creation steps for ECDSA signature (CCOP = 0b110000<i>0)", in section 25.5.2 (ECDSA signature) on page 756. Columns: OP STEP, MODE in PKA, GCMPH in SAES, Coupling or chaining, End-step event(1), CPU action in the step. 11 data row(s). Notes: 1. The application must clear and/or perform the described event for the CCB to automatically go to the next step.; 2. Once START bit is set SAES is reset, and OPERR linked to SAES are deactivated. Al.

rows:
– Enable the PKA in the correct mode, writing in PKA_CR 
MODE= 0x24 and EN=1 (repeat if EN bit stays clear). Wait 
for INITOK=1 in PKA_SR.
– Optionally decrypt the blob encryption key inthe SAES, 
using DHUK in 256-bit wrapped key mode.
– Set AES-GCM up in 256-bit encryption mode, with the 
DHUK or the decrypted key in register (if applicable).
– Write hash z in the PKA RAM.

– Complete GCM initialization in encryption mode. 
SAES_IVR1 to SAES_IVR3 are loaded with randoms.
– Read back blob IV in SAES_IVR registers.

Write ECC signature parameters in the PKA RAM, clearing 
CCF flags in the SAES triggered after each 2x32-bit write.

Write incrementally d in the PKA, using 0xCCB magic 
number. Values are drawn from the RNG. The PKA runs a 
special sanity check to verify random compliance with NIST 
standard (RNGERRF is set if sanity check fails).
Write incrementally d in the PKA.

– Read incrementally d from the PKA (writing 0xCCB magic 
numbers), and run AES encryption rounds. Special rule 
must be used for the last 64-bit word (see step 7 after the 
table).
– Read encrypted d in SAES_DOUTR. 
– Repeat for each 16 bytes block of data.

– Write incrementally k in the PKA, using 0xCCB magic 
number. Values are drawn from the RNG. The PKA runs a 
special sanity check to verify random compliance with 
NIST standard (RNGERRF is set if the sanity check fails).

– Complete GCM final.
– Read reference tag in the SAES.
– Start the operation in PKA setting START bit in PKA_CR
For the first two steps keep the SAES enabled (EN bit set).
The PKA computes the operation, PKA RAM reads as 0

– Read signature (r,s) in PKA RAM, and save it in SRAM. It 
is used (at least once) for blob creation verification.
– Set IPRST in CCB

– Clear the IPRST bit in CCB when CCB_BUSY and 
OPSTEP are cleared in CCB_SR.
– Verify the newly created blob, running the ECDSA 
signature blob use for public-key computation with it.
notes: 1. The application must clear and/or perform the described event for the CCB to automatically go to the next step.
2. Once START bit is set SAES is reset, and OPERR linked to SAES are deactivated. Also when START bit is set, CCB sets OPSTEP to 0x19 after a few cycles.
3. SAES cannot be used for any operations, for security reasons.
